newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil civil service reform on course for Wed vote.
newsitem.headline: Brazil civil service reform on course for Wed vote.

text.p: The Brazilian government's civil service reform bill is set for a first vote in the Chamber of Deputies Wednesday, although last-minute talks were scheduled to take place, a senior whip said.

Deputy Benito Gama said the constitutional amendment, which requires two three-fifths majorities in each house of Congress, would include a controversial ceiling on pay and benefits for public sector workers and pensioners.
The civil service reform aims to reduce spending on payrolls by limiting individual pay and benefits and allowing state and muncipal governments to dismiss currently unfireable workers.
Gama said the government would not bow to pressure within Congress to exempt lawmakers from the proposed 10,800-reais ($10,285) ceiling on pay and pensions.
A number of deputies who earn pensions from previous public sector posts and would lose out under the ceiling want to be exempted.
Gama said he did not believe news reports which said up to 140 of a total 513 deputies were in that situation and said talks would continue to find a solution to the potential impasse.

The whip also said the Chamber of Deputies was scheduled to vote Tuesday on a series of amendments to a bill regulating the opening up of the oil and gas industries to private capital. The bill was approved in the lower house last week.
